tagline: A self-hosted AI agent that investigates CI/CD failures

scenes.narration: Day 58: OpenSRE, a self-hosted agent that investigates CI failures, tested without any paid API key.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Reads CI logs to find the root cause of a failure
Separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones
Can push a fix to the PR branch for review
scenes.narration: OpenSRE reads failing CI logs, figures out whether the pipeline or the code is at fault, and can push a fix back to the pull request.

steps.narration: Before anything else, OpenSRE validates the configured LLM provider. With nothing set, it defaults to Anthropic.
Once validated, it builds a LangGraph state machine and gathers evidence in a plan actions node.
That node asks an LLM client what to check next. It can route to a local Ollama server instead of a cloud API, so no paid key is required.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Same command, same input. Setting LLM_PROVIDER=ollama was the only change.
scenes.narration: With no provider set, OpenSRE crashed on a raw Python traceback, since it silently defaults to Anthropic. Setting one variable, LLM_PROVIDER=ollama, let it reach the real LangGraph pipeline before failing on the network call.
Apache-2.0, self-hosted. Full write-up, sources and the Ollama follow-up on Zenn and GitHub.
